A statue that holds a mummified monk inside it is the subject of a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. Scans of an ancient Chinese Buddha statue revealed a seated human skeleton within, a monk who may have mummified himself through a grim ritual years long.

Rogan works through the discovery and the practice behind it, in which monks slowly starved and preserved their own bodies as acts of devotion. The talk asks what such faith asks of a person. The segment is a short, eerie piece of religious history, the kind of true oddity the show loves to pass along.
podcast-tuckercarlson-REEtJTqJbxI:
Journalist Matt Taibbi joins Tucker Carlson to discuss the secret files President Trump has been releasing. Taibbi, famous for his work on the Twitter Files, champions full declassification of government records. Here he argues for what should come out next.

Taibbi lists the files he most wants opened, from assassination records to intelligence abuses. He explains how secrecy protects officials more than it protects the country. Carlson asks whether Trump will really follow through against agency resistance. Curious viewers get a reporter's map of the vaults and a case for throwing them open.
